source_tasks.problem: The expression $7 -  7 +  5 -  7 -  7 \cdot  5 \times  5$ may be changed only by inserting parentheses; rearranging numbers or operations is not allowed. In total, how many values can be obtained?

observations: Both source questions fix an ordered sequence of operands and binary operators (+,-,*) and allow only full parenthesization (inserting parentheses) without reordering operands or operators.
The requested quantity is the number of distinct numerical values obtainable over all full binary parenthesizations of the fixed expression.
The interface supplies operands (integers) and operators (length = len(operands)-1), matching the fixed expression structure.
The mathematical core is: enumerate all full binary tree parenthesizations of the operator sequence, evaluate each under standard integer arithmetic, and count distinct results.
Duplicate values must be deduplicated; the count is of distinct values, not parenthesizations.
No semantic routing or task-ID dependence is needed; the procedure is purely combinatorial over the parameter arrays.
analysis.procedure_plan: Implement solve(parameters): read operands o[0..n-1] and operators op[0..n-2]. Use interval dynamic programming: for each subinterval [i,j] of operands, compute the set S[i][j] of all values obtainable by fully parenthesizing o[i..j] with operators op[i..j-1]. Base case S[i][i] = {o[i]}. For length L from 2 to n, for each i with j=i+L-1, for each split k in [i, j-1], combine every a in S[i][k] and b in S[k+1][j] using op[k]: if '+' add, if '-' subtract, if '*' multiply; insert results into S[i][j]. Return the cardinality of S[0][n-1]. Use exact integer arithmetic; sets handle deduplication. Complexity is O(n^3 * max set size), acceptable for n<=8.
analysis.uncertainty: Set sizes can grow but are bounded for n<=8 and small integer operands; no overflow concerns with standard integers. The procedure assumes standard precedence is irrelevant because all parenthesizations are enumerated, which matches the source framing. If the intended semantics required preserving default precedence rather than full parenthesization, the count would differ, but the source text explicitly allows inserting parentheses anywhere, so full parenthesization is the correct interpretation.

source_tasks.problem: The expression $7 -  7 +  5 -  7 -  7 \cdot  5 \times  5$ may be changed only by inserting parentheses; rearranging numbers or operations is not allowed. In total, how many values can be obtained?

Consider the expression $6 \cdot  7 \cdot  7 +  2 -  6 -  3 -  8$. Fully parenthesize it in every possible way without changing the order of numbers or operations. Parenthesizations with the same numerical result count only once. How many distinct values are possible?

response.applicability: Valid for 1 to 8 integer operands in [-10,20] and exactly len(operands)-1 operators drawn from +,-,*. Rejects malformed inputs, booleans, out-of-range operands, and wrong operator counts. Complexity grows with set sizes but is bounded for the stated limits.
response.description: Interval dynamic programming over the fixed operand/operator sequence. For each contiguous subinterval of operands, compute the set of all values obtainable by fully parenthesizing that subinterval. Combine sets across every split point using the operator at the split, deduplicating via sets. The answer is the size of the full-interval set. Exact integer arithmetic is used. Uncertainty: assumes the intended semantics is full parenthesization of the fixed sequence (no reordering, no precedence shortcuts), which matches the source framing.
